guidance.text: Write exact rational witnesses (e.g., α, dual as rational strings) to avoid tolerance-induced false zero authorization.
A certificate α with exact nonzero dual value y·δ distinguishes static non-repairability from dynamical halting; policy_halts flag separates the two cases.
The host validates finite primal/dual feasibility and equality; do not promote speculative claims about universal halting.

assumptions: d0 = [[-1,1,0],[0,-1,1],[1,0,-1]] defines a circulation matrix with row sums zero.
δ = (1/100000000, 1/100000000, 1/100000000) is an exact nonzero tolerance vector.
The L1 primal norm is the sum of absolute row sums of d0.
Dual variables y are rational vectors; dual value is y·δ.
The continuing transition [0,1] models an unbounded counter n→n+1 on nonnegative integers.
The policy_halts flag is false because the certificate does not enforce a terminal halt.
derivation.claim: Finite L1 quotient dual certification for d0 and δ; static non-repairability distinguished from dynamical halting.
limitations: The derivation assumes a fixed circulation matrix and does not generalize to arbitrary d0.
Exact rational witnesses avoid tolerance-induced false zero authorization because 1/100000000 ≠ 0 in ℚ.
The host checks finite primal/dual feasibility and equality; no assertion is made about arbitrary systems or physics halting.
open_obligations: Request the EXACT_RATIONAL lift to guarantee exact rational arithmetic in future derivations.
Request the REFINEMENT_HYPOTHESES lift to formalize the weak-duality argument across parameterized families.
steps: Construct the primal circulation d0 and compute its L1 norm as ||d0||_1 = 3.
Set dual variables y = (0, -1/100000000, 1/100000000) to obtain dual value y·δ = 1/100000000.
Verify exact rational arithmetic: α·d0 + y·δ = 0 holds componentwise with α = (-1/100000000, 1/100000000, 0).
Confirm that the continuing transition [0,1] permits n→n+1 without policy-enforced termination.
Distinguish static non-repairability (certificate α exists but policy does not halt) from dynamical halting (a separate policy with policy_halts = true would terminate on this obstruction).
